labelled_by: Claude (on behalf of Ruhan), by reading the code at the pinned commit; needs an independent second-person spot check

queries.text: BadSignature: Signature b'abc123' does not match

gold.why: signer.py raises BadSignature(f"Signature {sig!r} does not match", payload=value) when verify_signature fails.

queries.text: ValueError: The given separator cannot be used because it may be contained in the signature itself. ASCII letters, digits, and '-_=' must not be used.

gold.why: signer.py raises this exact ValueError when sep is in the base64 alphabet.
signer.py raises TypeError('Unknown key derivation method') in the final else branch of derive_key.

queries.text: BadPayload: Could not zlib decompress the payload before decoding the payload

gold.why: url_safe.py: wraps zlib.decompress failures into BadPayload with this message.

queries.text: A reset link that I wanted to be valid for one hour is still accepted a day later, as if the lifetime limit I passed to the loader was ignored.

gold.why: timed.py accepts max_age and forwards it to each signer's unsign.
timed.py: computes age = get_timestamp() - ts_int and raises SignatureExpired when age > max_age.

queries.text: Long payloads produce a token that begins with a dot; I do not understand how the library decides to shrink it and how it restores the original on the way back.

gold.why: url_safe.py: compresses with zlib when it saves more than one byte and prefixes '.' to flag compression.
url_safe.py: strips a leading '.' and decompresses before delegating to the base load_payload.

queries.text: After we replaced our application's secret with a new one, links that were mailed out before the change all stopped working at once.

gold.why: signer.py iterates over all configured secret keys (newest first) so that older keys still verify; with a single key old signatures fail.
signer.py normalises a single key or an iterable of keys into the secret_keys list used for rotation.

queries.text: I plugged in a custom encoder that produces raw bytes and now reading values back gives errors about decoding, although writing worked fine.

gold.why: serializer.py decodes the payload as UTF-8 text only when the serializer is a text serializer, else passes bytes through; mismatches raise BadPayload.
serializer.py decides text vs bytes by checking whether serializer.dumps({}) returns str.

queries.text: URLSafeTimedSerializer.loads(token, max_age=60) fails with a 'timestamp missing' error for a token that was created by URLSafeSerializer.dumps.

gold.why: timed.py (impl): raises BadTimeSignature('timestamp missing') when the unsigned result has no separator, i.e. the token was not produced by a timestamp signer.
timed.py sets TimestampSigner as the signer class, which is why the timed serializer expects a timestamp in the token.

queries.text: serializer.loads_unsafe(token) returns (False, None) for a string without any dot, even though I expected to see the payload.

gold.why: serializer.py: returns (False, None) when the BadSignature has payload None (no separator found), otherwise tries load_payload on e.payload.
signer.py raises BadSignature without payload when the separator is absent, which is what makes payload None.

queries.text: We want SHA-256 instead of the default hash for every signature our serializers create; where is the default digest chosen and how can it be overridden per serializer?

gold.why: signer.py class attribute naming the default digest (sha1 via _lazy_sha1).
signer.py accepts digest_method and falls back to default_digest_method.
serializer.py: instantiates the signer with **self.signer_kwargs, the per-serializer override path.

queries.text: Two services sign the same data with the same secret but different default salts so they reject each other's tokens; which defaults apply to salt and separator?

gold.why: signer.py defaults salt to b'itsdangerous.Signer' and sep to b'.'.
serializer.py defaults salt to b'itsdangerous' for the serializer (a different default than the signer).

queries.text: During a migration tokens signed with an older hash algorithm must still verify; how are fallback signers configured?

gold.why: serializer.py class-level default list of fallback signer parameters (empty since 2.0).
serializer.py: yields the main signer, then builds a signer for each fallback entry (dict, tuple or class).

queries.text: Tokens created with a custom salt cannot be loaded back with the default one although the secret key is identical; trace how the salt reaches the signing key.

gold.why: serializer.py: picks the salt (argument or self.salt) and passes it to the signer class.
serializer.py: the loads path builds signers with the salt given to loads, default self.salt.
signer.py mixes the salt into the derived key (concat / django-concat / hmac), so different salts give different keys.

queries.text: A token whose time stamp part is damaged raises Malformed timestamp; where is the time stamp encoded into the token and decoded again?

gold.why: timed.py: decodes ts_bytes with base64_decode and bytes_to_int and raises BadTimeSignature('Malformed timestamp').
encoding.py turns the packed 8-byte big-endian value back into an int.
encoding.py packs the timestamp int into bytes with leading zero bytes stripped; used by TimestampSigner.sign.
